title: GPU failure surface matrix & triage hitlist — draft
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, practical triage hitlist + failure-surface matrix for the most common GPU node instability modes we've seen in the last 12 months (ECC/correctable escalation, NVLink flakiness, driver OOMs/crashes, and kernel panics). Aim: help an on-call SRE get to a mitigative decision in 10–20 minutes and capture telemetry/notes for follow-up.

Status: draft. We expect to iterate with kernel-team and infra over the next 2 sprints.

Quick context (summary of observed modes):
- ECC noise: nodes show high correctable ECC counts on particular GPUs; if counts spike quickly, driver may escalate and device resets happen leading to container OOMs. Often correlated with heavy memory-bound batch workloads.
- NVLink error spikes: NVLink CRC/transport errors reported for a subset of link pairs; errors sometimes transient after cold-restart but can persist across reboots. Heavy allreduce/comms jobs amplify.
- NVIDIA driver crashes: nvidia-persistenced / nvidia-driver processes crash with SIGSEGV after specific kernel/driver combos (notably driver 545.x + kernel 6.1.x in our fleet).
- Kernel panic: rare, often preceded by OOM-killer events or GPU reset loops; requires full node repro and hardware diagnosis.

Immediate triage checklist (10–20 min):
1) Surface alert and scope
   - Which node(s) are affected? (nodename(s) from alert)
   - Are pods failing with GPU errors or node-level NotReady?
   - Impact: how many replicas, which customers?

2) Live signal snapshot (commands to run):
   - kubectl get nodes | grep <node>
   - kubectl describe node <node>  # look for kernel crash messages, docker/containerd errors
   - ssh root@<node> -- sudo journalctl -b --no-pager | tail -n 200
   - sudo dmesg | tail -n 200  # kernel logs for GPU resets/panic traces
   - nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,PRODUCT,FB memory  # ECC counters and memory errors
   - nvidia-smi topo -m  # NVLink topology and link states
   - sudo cat /proc/driver/nvidia/params  # driver params in use
   - kubectl logs <pod> -n <ns> --previous | tail -n 200  # capture container-level GPU errors

3) Quick heuristics and triage outcomes
   - If ECC correctable counters are rising on a single GPU but node stable: mark GPU as suspect; cordon node and drain non-critical pods from that node; schedule targeted workload re-run onto other nodes.
   - If NVLink CRC errors present and affect multi-GPU jobs: failover multi-GPU jobs to single-GPU variants or other nodes; restrict jobs with heavy NCCL/allreduce until link health cleared.
   - If driver process crashes (dmesg shows nvidia_uvm or nvidia_drm SIGSEGV): collect driver version, kernel version; attempt graceful GPU service restart (see mitigations), escalate to infra if repeating across nodes.
   - If kernel panic: escalate immediately to on-call infra + hardware ops and initiate node evacuation; collect as much printk/dmesg and vmcore if automatic capture available.

Signals to collect (copy/paste queries):
- ECC counters: nvidia-smi -q -d ECC | egrep "Total|Current|Single-bit|Double-bit" -A3
- NVLink errors: sudo cat /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/0000:$(lspci | grep NVIDIA | awk '{print $1}' | head -n1)/nvlink.h  # fallback if available
- kernel OOPS patterns: sudo journalctl -k -b | egrep "NVRM|nvidia|GPU|nvlink|BUG|panic|oom" -A3 -B3

Typical mitigations (fast, reversible):
- Cordoning and draining node: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- Restart NVIDIA services: sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced && sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm && sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm && sudo systemctl restart kubelet  # note: may evict pods
- Reboot node if driver/firmware state appears corrupted and service restart didn't help. Prefer controlled reboot during maintenance window if impact is moderate; emergency reboot if kernel panic/IO hangs persist.
- For NVLink: reduce multi-GPU assignment by setting device-affinity env vars or job constraints (temporary scheduler patch to avoid placement on nodes with >=1 link error).

Detailed runbook sketch (for inclusion in consolidated playbook):
Step A: Confirm and isolate
- Take node out of scheduler (cordon).
- Snapshot /var/log/messages, journalctl, dmesg, nvidia-smi outputs to S3 (linkify below).
- Tag incident with GPU serial(s) and driver/kernel versions.
Step B: Attempt soft recovery
- Restart nvidia-persistenced and uvm module as above.
- If containerized CUDA workloads, restart runtime on affected pods (kubectl delete pod <pod> -n <ns> to force reschedule).
- Re-run failing job on a different node; if job succeeds, mark as transient.
Step C: Escalate and hardware actions
- If ECC counts continue to grow after multiple reboots or errors map to same GPU channel, open a hardware ticket with vendor including ECC counter dumps and timestamps.
- For nvlink persistent errors across reboots, request NVLink cable/hardware swap and test using vendor diagnostics.

Log snippets and patterns to search for in previous incidents:
- "NVRM: Xid (PCI-DMA): 31"  -> memory access errors (device reset likely)
- "NVRM: RmProcessInfoDestroy" followed by "nvidia_uvm: GPU lockup" -> driver-level hang
- "nvlink: crc error" or "NVLINK: channel.*error" -> link CRC/transport errors
- "kernel panic - not syncing: OOM killer terminated" -> node-level kernel panic context

On-call notes (real example from 2025-03-10 23:12 PST):
- Observed alert: large NCCL job failing across 3 nodes in cluster-gpu-3 pool.
- Quick check: nvidia-smi showed ECC correctable counts rising on GPU0 of nodes node-13 and node-14, but node-15 showed NVLink CRC errors on link 1-2.
- Action: cordoned node-13 and node-14, restarted nvidia-persistenced on both. Jobs rescheduled and succeeded on node-21. Node-15 required full reboot; NVLink errors persisted after reboot. Raised ticket SRE-1428 and attached nvlink dumps.
- Follow-up: vendor diagnostics run by hardware-ops identified degraded NVLink interposer on node-15; replacement scheduled.

Post-incident data to attach (what to collect every time):
- /var/log/messages, /var/log/kern.log for last 2 boots
- nvidia-smi -q output for each GPU (store as .txt)
- dmesg output and journalctl -k -b dump
- Kubernetes pod logs for affected jobs with --previous
- diag tar from vendor tools when requested

Open questions / hypotheses to validate:
- Are specific kernel/driver combos (e.g., 545.x + kernel 6.1) correlated to the majority of our crashes? We need fleetwide telemetry by kernel/driver over last 6 months.
- Does a particular PCI-e lane or riser board map to repeated ECC spikes? Cross-check hardware mapping with serials.
- Could aggressive multi-job consolidation (bin-packing) be increasing temperatures and accelerating ECC events? Need temp telemetry near GPU sensors.

Suggested engineering follow-ups (owners):
- infra/sre: add a metric pipeline for fleetwide ECC correctable count per-GPU (owner: Arjun).
- platform: add job placement rule to avoid multi-GPU jobs on nodes with recent NVLink errors for 24h (owner: Lena).
- hw-ops: create a swap-and-verify checklist for NVLink interposers and riser swaps (owner: Tomás).

Quick reference: useful Slack channels and runbook links
- #sre-gpu (ops channel)
- #hw-ops (hardware escalations)
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/INC-2025-GPU-PLAY

Appendix: short example queries for observability
- Fleet query: sum by (driver_version) (increase(nvidia_ecc_correctable_total[30d]))  # returns ECC trends by driver
- Node health query: max_over_time(node_gpu_temperature_celsius[1h]) > 85  # candidate overheating nodes
- NVLink errors: increase(nvidia_nvlink_crc_errors_total[1d]) > 0  # nodes to quarantine

Notes to reviewer:
This is intentionally compact and action-oriented. Next iteration should fold in vendor diagnostic commands and a sample incident timeline template for postmortem consumption. Also want SLOs for mean time to remediate NVLink vs ECC vs driver crash classes.

End of draft.
